submission.justification: R3 gave the highest simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c at every thickness scanned. At 3 cm its separation was 4.6, against 3.8 for R2 and 2.9 for R1. A finer scan of R3 peaked at 3.2 cm with a separation of 4.781. The R3 curve is somewhat irregular (2.8 cm gives 4.345, 3.5 cm gives 4.596), so the exact optimum is uncertain. The 3.2 cm choice is still within the 1–6 cm limit and sits in the best-performing 3–3.5 cm region. The recorded results contain no lifetime or degradation data for any radiator, so I could not verify the lifetime constraint. The 2025 values equal the baseline values. That constraint should be checked against candidate_specs.md and the project documents before this choice is final.

requirements.requirement: Best possible pi/K separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 at 3.2 cm gives 4.781, the highest of all simulated options. The best R2 value is 3.8 and the best R1 value is 2.9.

requirements.requirement: Radiator is one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: R3 is one of Radiator-R1, R2 and R3.

requirements.requirement: Radiator keeps its performance over the experiment's lifetime
requirements.evidence: No lifetime or aging results were recorded. The only year-tagged values are the 2025 ones at 3 cm (R3 4.6, R2 3.8, R1 2.9), which match the baseline values. Long-term degradation was not assessed.
3.2 cm is within the 1–6 cm range.

requirements.requirement: Submit one recommended radiator and thickness
requirements.evidence: This submission recommends R3 at 3.2 cm.
